definitions.event_count_scope: full ns-3 lifecycle matched to offered BQO1 hashes; bounded_window is reported separately
definitions.events_per_delivered: full matched lifecycle events divided by unique application deliveries
definitions.lag_attribution: positive increase at the next pre-serialization lag sample attributed to the previous event; negative catch-up is not netted
definitions.observed_ingress: unique packets with an ns-3 ingress event, independent of policy admission
definitions.policy_admission: unique packets with an explicit ns-3 admit event; never inferred from offered attempts
definitions.rate_time_bases: offered_window_normalized uses configured source duration; profile_wall_interval includes bounded drain
definitions.scheduler_lag: host monotonic elapsed minus ns-3 simulation elapsed, sampled at every ns-3 event in the bounded window

root_cause.largest_amplifier: legacy baseline used the vendored ns-3 SetBackoffParams fourth/fifth argument mismatch, leaving the old fifth argument as maxRetries=1000000; 45927 rich backoff lifecycle rows amplified the backlog
root_cause.legacy_per_event_cost: each lifecycle callback reparsed and SHA-256-hashed the frame, serialized roughly 2 KiB of JSON, and synchronously flushed the stream
root_cause.mechanism: unbounded offered traffic entered ingress/Sionna/queue work before capacity admission
root_cause.primary: baseline positive scheduler-lag growth is dominated by work following the 'ingress' callback; see the attributed positive growth and same-simulation-time evidence
root_cause.serial_not_primary: baseline BSF1 evidence is one fragment per serial record

serial.decision: aggregation remains disabled: BSF1 has no fragmentation fan-out (1 -> 1 fragments/record), and the hash-matched overload lag attribution contains no BSF1 lifecycle; this does not claim that individual serial records are large
serial.overload_event_scope: BQO1 logical-packet hashes only; BSF1 serial records are excluded from the scheduler-lag attribution
